abstract: Adeno associated virus (AAV)-mediated gene therapy holds great promise for curing various diseases, but uncontrolled expression of transgenes in both healthy and diseased cells driven by constitutively active general promoters is a potential safety risk. Controlled gene therapy can be achieved using a disease-responsive promoter (DRP) that drives expression of a therapeutic gene only in diseased cells and shuts off once the cells become healthy again. We used correlative analysis of ATAC-seq and ncRNA-seq of healthy and diseased retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) to identify and characterize two DRPs that possess unique DRP activities in two mouse models of optic neuropathy. We further optimized one DRP to generate DRP-3L2, which has minimum promoter activity in naïve healthy RGCs, but drives potent neuroprotective gene expression in diseased RGCs and then abates after RGCs are protected and returning to health. Our proof-of-concept studies demonstrate that DRP-mediated precisely controlled gene therapy provides a new and promising neuroprotective strategy for CNS axonopathies.
